translations.source_sense_description: затруднительное положение, неприятное или хлопотливое происшествие

glosses: To draw (an object, especially a sharp or angular one), along (something) while exerting pressure.

examples.text: She scraped the wooden plate with her fingernails.
That car often scrapes the shallowest of humps because of its low ground clearance.

glosses: To remove (something) by drawing an object along in this manner.

examples.text: Scrape the chewing gum off with a knife.

glosses: To injure or damage by rubbing across a surface.

examples.text: She tripped on a rock and scraped her knee.
We went tip-toeing along a path amongst the trees back towards the end of the widow's garden, stooping down so as the branches wouldn't scrape our heads.

glosses: To barely manage to achieve or attain.

examples.text: I scraped a pass in the exam.

glosses: To collect or gather, especially without regard to the quality of what is chosen.

examples.text: Just use whatever you can scrape together.

glosses: To extract data by automated means from a format not intended to be machine-readable, such as a screenshot or a formatted web page.

examples.text: They didn't provide an API, so I simply scraped their website.

The threat of the impending axe horrified Scott. He and his supporters hastily “scraped” as many Geocities^([sic]) pages as they could, creating a 641-gigabyte archive that initially circulated on file-sharing networks.

glosses: To occupy oneself with getting laboriously.

examples.text: He scraped and saved until he became rich.
And he shall spend mine honour with his shame, As thriftless sons their scraping fathers' gold

glosses: To play awkwardly and inharmoniously on a violin or similar instrument.

examples.text: Some people covered their ears when he started to scrape his violin.
At that time the Grand Duke had only two occupations. One was to scrape the violin, the other to train spaniels for hunting.

glosses: To draw back the right foot along the ground or floor when making a bow.

examples.text: Yossarian went along in Milo Minderbinder's speeding M & M staff car to police headquarters to meet a swarthy, untidy police commissioner with a narrow black mustache and unbuttoned tunic who was fiddling with a stout woman with warts and two chins when they entered his office and who greeted Milo with warm surprise and bowed and scraped in obscene servility as though Milo were some elegant marquis.

glosses: To express disapprobation of (a play, etc.) or to silence (a speaker) by drawing the feet back and forth upon the floor; usually with down.

examples.text: When the debate was resumed, the tide ran so strongly against the accused that his friends were coughed and scraped down.

glosses: A broad, shallow injury left by scraping (rather than a cut or a scratch).

examples.text: He fell on the sidewalk and got a scrape on his knee.

glosses: The sound or action of something being scraped.

examples.text: For a long while, the only sounds in the café were the scrapes of forks against old white plates and occasional slurps from coffee mugs.
The scrape of the plate against the stone woke him, and he looked across to find Isocrates there, replacing the food.

glosses: Something removed by being scraped; a thin layer of something such as butter on bread.

glosses: A fight, especially a fistfight without weapons.

examples.text: He got in a scrape with the school bully.
